checkpoints.description: [1/3] Plan: Android share target for one or many images/videos; reuse hash-first /api/has + /api/upload; settings screen Test connection against /api/status; build, sign and serve the updated APK; README/ADR-025

impact_assessment.why: Android users can schedule a sync but cannot send a chosen photo from Gallery without opening Harbor first
impact_assessment.benefits: One share action uploads selected photos with the same verified protocol; connection test catches a wrong address or key before a sync
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new exported ShareActivity and intent filters; dependency: none; concurrency: share upload and background job can overlap but each file is hash-checked; state: no new persistence
impact_assessment.mitigation: Use the same hash-before-upload path, skip already-present files, keep a simple status screen, and rebuild/sign/verify the APK

checkpoints.description: [2/3] Exported ShareActivity for SEND/SEND_MULTIPLE image/video; metadata fallback, SHA-256 -> /api/has -> /api/upload, skips present files; Test calls /api/status; rebuilt signed APK 57,814 bytes with ShareActivity filters
[3/3] README/android README/ADR-025; server APK byte-identical after rebuild; 151 tests stable across 4 runs; 4/4 gates; checklists: passed
Task 'android-share' completed successfully.

[1/2] Plan: accept Intent.getData() when a share arrives without EXTRA_STREAM/ClipData; rerun the APK on an Android 14 emulator against a real Harbor for Test, first sync, duplicate sync and share; document the evidence

impact_assessment.why: The emulator proved the main sync, but an explicit data-URI share was not handled; the app also had no hardware-level verification record
impact_assessment.benefits: Share intents from more providers work; the APK has a reproducible end-to-end check; no server or schema change
impact_assessment.risks: contract: one more share fallback; dependency: none; concurrency: hash checks already deduplicate; state: none
impact_assessment.mitigation: Use the existing hash-first upload path, keep data URIs last after EXTRA_STREAM and ClipData, and record the exact emulator results in the Android README

checkpoints.description: [2/2] Emulator Android 14: Test Connected, first sync 1 sent, second 0 sent/1 already, share 1 sent; server catalog saw both PNGs; data-URI fallback documented; 151 tests, 4/4 gates; checklists: passed
Task 'android-e2e' completed successfully.
[1/1] Verify the scheduled JobService on Android 14: enable the 6-hour background switch, confirm PERSISTED/NOT_METERED/PERIODIC in dumpsys, force-run the job and see the MediaStore images arrive

impact_assessment.why: The periodic path had only been compiled; only the manual sync and share paths were exercised
impact_assessment.benefits: Confirms Android actually schedules and executes the background upload without the app in front
impact_assessment.risks: contract: none; dependency: none; concurrency: forced job overlaps the app UI but hash checks deduplicate; state: none
impact_assessment.mitigation: Use the persisted job already declared in the manifest, force-run through the system scheduler, and verify the server catalog

checkpoints.description: [1/1] dumpsys showed JOB #u0a192/1 PERSISTED NOT_METERED PERIODIC +6h; forced run uploaded 3 MediaStore images; documented in android/README; 151 tests, 4/4 gates
Task 'android-bg-verify' completed successfully.

[1/3] Plan: build.py writes Harbor.apk.json next to the signed APK with version, versionCode, size, SHA-256 and build time; /android/Harbor.apk.json serves it; install page displays it; tests, README, ADR-026

impact_assessment.why: The APK download is a binary with no visible version or checksum, so a user cannot tell what they are installing or whether the bytes changed
impact_assessment.benefits: Verifiable sideload downloads; the page identifies the exact build; no server schema or runtime dependency
impact_assessment.risks: contract: one generated sidecar and a public JSON route; dependency: hashlib/json only; concurrency: metadata written after signing; state: one small file beside the APK
impact_assessment.mitigation: Generate metadata only after the signed APK is verified, serve it no-cache, show the full SHA-256, and test both present and missing sidecar cases

checkpoints.description: [2/3] build.py writes Harbor.apk.json after apksigner verify (version/code/size/sha256/built_at); /android/Harbor.apk.json served no-cache; install page displays it; HTTP test and byte/checksum dogfood
[3/3] README/android README/ADR-026; 151 tests; 4/4 gates; served page/APK/metadata all 200 with matching SHA-256; checklists: passed
Task 'apk-metadata' completed successfully.

[1/2] Plan: app reads /android/Harbor.apk.json on launch, compares versionCode with the installed build, shows Update Harbor and opens the install page when newer; keep the existing Test/sync/share paths; rebuild, emulator-check, README/ADR-027

impact_assessment.why: The APK page now carries a version, but the installed app has no way to notice that the server has a newer build
impact_assessment.benefits: Users can see an update is available without manually comparing versions; reuses the public metadata route
impact_assessment.risks: contract: one public metadata read from the app; dependency: none; concurrency: launch-time background check only; state: none
impact_assessment.mitigation: Treat a missing or malformed sidecar as no update, compare integer versionCode, and only show the button when the served code is newer

checkpoints.description: [2/2] App reads Harbor.apk.json on launch, compares versionCode and shows Update Harbor; emulator with a temporary versionCode 2 showed 'Harbor 2 is available' and the button; metadata restored to 1.0; 151 tests, 4/4 gates; README/ADR-027; checklists: passed
Task 'android-update' completed successfully.

[1/3] Plan: 192/512 PNG icons, manifest entries, /sw.js with root scope, network-first shell caching and API/media bypass, registration in index.html; service-worker and icon tests; Playwright registration dogfood; README/ADR-028

impact_assessment.why: Android users can install the APK, but the browser gallery itself cannot be installed to the home screen as a standalone app
impact_assessment.benefits: One-tap PWA install on Android/Chrome; cached shell opens offline; photos and API stay network-only and private
impact_assessment.risks: contract: public /sw.js, static icons and manifest; dependency: none; concurrency: service worker updates asynchronously; state: cache storage on the device
impact_assessment.mitigation: Serve /sw.js no-cache with Service-Worker-Allowed, use network-first so online clients see fresh assets, bypass /api, /media and /thumb, and delete old caches on activate

checkpoints.description: [2/3] 192/512 icons, manifest entries, /sw.js root-scope no-cache, network-first shell cache with API/media bypass, registration moved to app.js (CSP-safe); HTTP test and Chromium SW registration/controller dogfood
